opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Black (employee ID E008) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E008.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Full-time Payroll Specialist requested admin to Source Code. Admin is only available to the role that owns the system (Engineer), so the maximum for this employee is write. Recommending write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E008 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read without advanced training; admin is never allowed. Requested admin to Source Code exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Karen Black (E008) requested admin access to Source Code. Admin is only permitted for full-time employees whose role owns the system (Engineer), and this employee is a Payroll Specialist, so admin is not allowed. There is a conflict in the notes: HR lists the employee as full-time (max write), while Security lists the employee as a contractor with basic security training (max read). Since admin exceeds the maximum under either interpretation, and read is the only level that satisfies both notes' policy limits, I grant the safe maximum of read.
